newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nippon Oil, Idemitsu to cooperate in petrol supply.
newsitem.headline: Nippon Oil, Idemitsu to cooperate in petrol supply.

text.p: Refiners Nippon Oil Co Ltd and Idemitsu Kosan Co Ltd said on Monday they plan to expand their cooperation in domestic oil product distribution to gasoline next year.
The firms have already been cooperating in the distribution of asphalt, heavy fuel oil, kerosene and gas oil in order to cut costs.

From early next year, Nippon Oil will supply gasoline to Idemitsu petrol stations located near Nippon Oil terminals, and vice versa, although the agreement will not initially include the northern island of Hokkaido, a Nippon Oil spokesman said.

The cooperation will become possible as Nippon Oil plans to commission benzene removal units at its 385,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) Negishi refinery, near Tokyo, in January 1998, bringing the benzene content of its gasoline into line with that of Idemitsu's, he said.

The cooperation in gasoline supply is expected to be extended to cover Hokkaido in fiscal 2000/01 following the installation of similar units at Nippon Oil's 170,000 bpd Muroran refinery on the island in fiscal 1999/2000, he said.

The spokesman said the cooperation in domestic distribution would save the two firms about five billion yen each in fiscal 2000/01, when the volume of oil products supplied to each other is expected to reach five million kilolitres.
Both firms denied persistent market rumours that the close ties between them will eventually lead to a full-scale merger.
